html:
The Canichana are an Indigenous people of the Moxos plains of Beni, Bolivia, on the Mamoré and Machupo rivers. Their language may be an isolate, unrelated to any other.

Spanish accounts describe them as warlike and feared by their neighbours. In the late 1600s Jesuits gathered them into the mission of San Pedro, which became the main town of the Moxos missions. After the Jesuits were expelled in 1767 the missions declined. In 1991 about 500 Canichana people were counted; by 2000 nobody spoke the language as a first tongue. Their neighbours included the Itonama, Cayubaba and Movima.
